Authenticated IDOR/BFLA hunting on https://worknet.rizzgm.xyz app API, using a legitimate low-priv identity only. Context: Next.js on Vercel, session cookie is session=<64hex> (tokens plaintext-leaked in Supabase sessions table — wiki note 56ea4f + finding 12d1d9 have endpoint map + a leaked token; /api/bootstrap proves auth works with it). llms.txt documents API surface: /api/jobs*, /api/profile, /api/agents/register|execute-transaction|{id}/reputation, /api/jobs/{id}/apply|submit|upload-task, /api/wallet/*, /api/indexer/sync (x-admin-secret), x402 paid endpoints.
Strict rules: RATE 1 req/3s max, curl only, single browser session allowed via agent-browser --session appapi (WAF trips on bursts, ~10min cooldown burn). NEVER touch /api/indexer/sync (admin secret brute = out of scope). No scanner tools against this host. No destructive actions (no deleting others' jobs/applications; create nothing unless needed for validation chain, then clean up own artifacts).
Hunt list:
1. Session robustness with leaked token: expired-token acceptance, session cookie Secure/HttpOnly flags, logout invalidation (do NOT log out other users' sessions — with own synthetic flow only if possible; if leaked token logout affects victim, skip).
2. IDOR: /api/jobs/{id} enumeration for other users' submissions, apply/submit/upload-task accepting attacker-controlled submitterProfileId/ownerProfileId (per llms.txt these are client-supplied), /api/agents/{id}/reputation injection or cross-account read.

4. Business logic: job pricing/escrow state tamper via well-formed requests; duplicate application; self-apply.
File each confirmed separate vuln via create_vulnerability_report with proxy http_exchange_ids, severity per real impact (IDOR high/critical based on data sensitivity). record_coverage each surface tested. agent_finish with open_items for anything WAF-blocked or needing a wallet identity you lack.

entries.surface: pactum_session cookie (Set-Cookie attrs) + POST/PUT API routes
entries.risk_area: CSRF via cross-site state-change (SameSite=Lax cookie attribute)
entries.evidence: pactum_session cookie issued with HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=lax+Path=/+Max-Age=604800 (request 4107 response header). SameSite=lax withholds cookie on cross-site POST/PUT subresource requests (fetch/XHR/form). Only state-changing routes observed are POST/PUT/session-bordered; no state-mutating GET route documented in the Pactum API surface. Without a state-changing GET route, no PoC achievable to demonstrate cookie riding on cross-site state change; Deemed not exploitable at present.

entries.risk_area: Cookie-parser normalization / duplicate-cookie handling (last-wins)
entries.evidence: Cookie name-case differential: `Pactum_Session` capitalized variant returned 200 (matching valid sig in value), and duplicate-cookie `pactum_session=garbage; pactum_session=<valid>` also returned 200 (last-wins). Confirms parser's name-normalization and last-wins dedup; no direct security impact by itself (valid signature still required) but worth flagging in report as defense-in-depth weakness.

entries.risk_area: Session HMAC forging / signature binding / timestamp manipulation
entries.evidence: Definitive reforge with freshly-issued uid2 session (15:01, forge-final run 4169–4171): POSCTRL fresh uid2 own=200; FORGED uid1+uid2fresh_ts+uid2fresh_sig=401 (4170, cookie verified); NEGCTRL corrupted-sig=401 (4171). Signature is bound to (uid,ts) with a server secret — cross-user sig re-use fails even with fresh pair. Earlier one-off 200 (4084) unreproducible; logged as transient anomaly, not exploited.

entries.risk_area: Cross-tenant IDOR via session-scoped routes (acct2/3 vs acct1)
entries.evidence: 4 accounts live across the run; policy/invoice/summary sessions scoped per-uid; cross-account (acct2/acct3/fresh-uid2-sig) attempts to read or mutate uid1's data all 401/rejected (requests 4101–4105, 4113, 4166, 4167, 4170); policies PUT with injected user/project identifiers stayed owner-bound (4154–4156). Not tested: invoice-specific BOLA by invoice-ID (no authed invoice creation succeeded due to 402-fund gate — requires funded state channel).

gaps.surface: learning.rizzgm.xyz pre-existing account takeover depth (beyond read-level verification)
gaps.risk_area: Account impersonation beyond read-level check + backend deletion integrity
gaps.detail: Overwriting wrong surface label on entry 7b9771: actual surface is learning.rizzgm.xyz users_learn backend deletion integrity — anon REST DELETE returns 204 but rows persist (verified on 8 synthetic rows across id/username filters, table count 44→45 never decreasing); possible trigger/security-definer protection or PostgREST quirk. Existing-user impersonation itself IS confirmed at read level inside vuln-0003 (Shreeju). Two gaps remain open: exact DELETE no-op mechanism, and whether it guards against write-level actions on adopted accounts.
